Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:1.hebrew: משום צובע - שצובע את הבשר של בית השחיטה, ולקמן מפרש אמאי מיכוין לצובעו. וצביעה הואי במשכן אב מלאכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:1.english: Due to dyeing - For he dyes the meat of the slaughter area, and below [the Gemara] explains why he intends to dye it. And dyeing was a primary category of labor in the Tabernacle.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:2.hebrew: משום נטילת נשמה - דנטילת נשמה הואי במשכן — באילים מאדמים, ותחש וחלזון:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:2.english: Due to taking a life - For taking a life took place in the Mishkan — in [the case of] the red-dyed rams, the tachash, and the chilazon.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:3.hebrew: צובע בשר במאי ניחא ליה - להאי שוחט בצביעת הבשר — היינו חוכא, ואני אומר בו טעם:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:3.english: Dyeing meat, in what [way] is it pleasing to him - [How is it pleasing] to this slaughterer in the dyeing of the meat? That is the mockery, and [so] I am stating a reason for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:4.english: Due to dyeing as well - And the practical difference is to hold him liable for two [transgressions].

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:5.hebrew: מילתא דאמרי אימא כו' - דבר תימה אמרתי להזכיר צביעה בשחיטה. צריך אני לומר בו דבר טעם, דלא ליתו דרי בתראי — השומעים — וליחכו עלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:5.english: [Regarding] the statement that I said, I will say, etc. - I said an astonishing thing in mentioning dyeing in [connection with] slaughter. I must state a reasoned explanation for it, so that later generations — who hear [it] — will not come and laugh at me.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:6.english: It is pleasing to him that the place of slaughter be soiled with blood - That it be dyed with blood.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:7.hebrew: כי היכי דניחזייה אינשי - שנשחטה היום, וניתו ונזבנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:1:7.english: So that people will see it - That it was slaughtered today, and they will come and buy.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:2:1.english: Salting is the same as tanning - Is salting not a requirement of tanning?

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:2:2.hebrew: ועייל שירטוט - לפי שדרך הרצענין, כשהוא בא לחתכו, משרטטו תחלה כפי מה שהוא רוצה להאריך ולהרחיב ולקצר החיתוך, ואחר כך מעביר הסכין דרך השירטוט. וכן בעורות המשכן, כשחתכום:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:2:2.english: And introduce scoring - Because it is the practice of leatherworkers, when one comes to cut [a hide], he first scores it according to how he wishes to lengthen, widen, or shorten the cut, and afterwards he passes the knife along the scoring; and likewise with the hides of the Mishkan, when they cut them.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:2:3.english: When he needs it for a journey - For he salts it heavily.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:1.hebrew: השף בין העמודים - כגון עמודי אכסדראות שעשוים חלונות חלונות, ונסמכין בחלונות בין עמוד לעמוד; והשף שם בקרקעית הבנין שנשענין עליו כדי שיהא חלק — חייב משום ממחק:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:1.english: One who rubs between the pillars - For example, pillars of porticos that are made [with] window-like openings, and [people] lean in the openings between pillar and pillar; and one who rubs there on the base of the structure that they lean upon, so that it will be smooth, is liable due to [the labor of] smoothing.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:2.english: One who planes the tops of posts - So that their tops will be even and pointed.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:3.english: One who spreads a bandage - He smooths a bandage over the wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:4.hebrew: מסתת את האבן - לאחר שנעקרה מן ההר ונחצבה, מחליקה:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:4.english: One who chisels the stone - After it was detached from the mountain and hewn, he smooths it.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:5.english: Due to striking with a hammer - For it is the completion of the labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:6.english: One who forms a figure on a vessel - [This applies] to a vessel that is designated for this, to beautify it.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:7.hebrew: מנפח בכלי זכוכית - כשהותך, נעשה על ידי נפוח:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:7.english: One who blows a glass vessel - Once [the glass] has been melted, it is formed by means of blowing.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:8.hebrew: דשקיל אקופי - ראשי חוטין התלויין ביריעה במקום קשורין כשניתק בה חוט וקשרוהו, וכן קשין וקסמים דקין שנארגו בה בלא מתכוין, ונוטלין אותם ממנה לאחר אריגה — גמר מלאכה הוא, וחייב משום מכה בפטיש:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:3:8.english: [One] who removes akuffei - The ends of threads hanging from the fabric at the place of knots when a thread snapped in it and they tied it; and likewise bits of straw and thin splinters that were woven into it unintentionally, and one removes them from it after weaving — this is the completion of the work, and he is liable due to [the labor of] striking with a hammer.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:4:1.hebrew: כתב אות אחת גדולה כו' פטור - שבקרשי המשכן שתים היו כותבים, אחת בזו ואחת בזו, כדי לזווגן כשסותרים אותן:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:4:1.english: One who wrote one large letter, etc., is exempt - For on the planks of the Mishkan they would write two [letters], one on this [plank] and one on that [plank], in order to pair them when they dismantled them.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:4:2.hebrew: מחק אות אחת כו' חייב - שאין מלאכת מחיקה חשובה אלא ע"מ לכתוב, והרי יש מקום לשתי אותיות:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:4:2.english: One who erased one letter, etc., is liable - For the labor of erasing is significant only in order to write, and behold, there is room for two letters.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:4:3.hebrew: אמר רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי - הא קמ"ל: מאן תנא קמא — ר' מנחם ברבי יוסי:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:4:3.english: Rabbi Menaḥem, son of Rabbi Yosei, said - This comes to teach us who the first Tanna is: Rabbi Menaḥem, son of Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:1.hebrew: לאפוקי מדרבי אליעזר - דהא אמרן, דלא נמנו כאן אלא להודיענו מנין חטאות של העלם אחד. ותנא "הרי אלו" למעוטי, שאם עשה תולדותיהם עמהן — דאינו מביא עליהן חטאת; ודלא כרבי אליעזר, דמחייב אתולדה עם האב בכריתות:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:1.english: To exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Eliezer - For we said that they were enumerated here only to inform us of the number of sin-offerings for a single lapse of awareness; and [the Tanna] taught "These [are]" to exclude [additional sin-offerings, teaching] that if one performed their subcategories along with them, he does not bring a sin-offering for them — and not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who holds [one] liable for a subcategory [performed] together with the primary category, in [tractate] Keritot.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:2.english: Lining up - He evens out the warp [threads] with a karkar, which is called reiol [spindle].

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:3.hebrew: מדקדק - כשמותח חוט הערב, מכה בכרכר עליו במקומות מקומות ליישבו, שלא יהא מתוח יותר מדאי, שהמתיחה מעכבתו מהתחבר יפה עם הארג:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:3.english: Beating - When he stretches the thread of the weft, he strikes upon it with a weaver's pin in various places to settle it, so that it will not be overly taut, for the tension prevents it from joining well with the woven fabric.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:4.hebrew: שובט הרי הוא בכלל מיסך - דהיינו מיסך ממש, שמסדר חוטי השתי:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:4.english: Lining up is subsumed under warping - That is, it is actual warping, since he arranges the threads of the warp.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:5.hebrew: הרי הוא אורג - דהיינו אורג ממש, ולא דמי לזורה ובורר ומרקד, דזה בקשין, וזה בצרורות, וזה בקמח:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:6:5.english: Behold, it is weaving - For that is actual weaving, and it is not similar to winnowing, selecting, and sifting, for this [one is] with straw, this [one is] with pebbles, and this [one is] with flour.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:7:1.english: Anything fit to store - That it is a type [of item] used for human need.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:7:2.hebrew: ומצניעין כמוהו - כמות זה, כלומר שיש בו שיעור הראוי להצניעו:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:7:2.english: And [people] store [items] like it - An amount like this — that is to say, that it has a measure fit to be stored.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:7:3.hebrew: אין חיוב אלא למצניעו - אם נעשה חביב לאדם א' והצניעו, חייב על הוצאתו אם חזר והוציאו; אבל אדם אחר אינו חייב עליו, דלגביה לאו מלאכה הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:7:3.english: There is liability only for the one who stored it - If it became dear to one person and he stored it, he is liable for carrying it out if he subsequently carried it out; but another person is not liable for it, as with respect to him, it is not an [act of] labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:8:1.hebrew: מ"ד דם נדה - אינו כשר להצניע, כ"ש עצי אשרה — דאיסורי הנאה נינהו ומאיסי, וצריך לאבדן:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:8:1.english: The one who said menstrual blood - [holds that it] is not fit to store; all the more so the wood of an ashera, as they are forbidden for benefit and are repulsive, and one must destroy them.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:8:2.hebrew: כיון דחלשא - המאכיל דם האדם לחתול, נעשה חלש אותו אדם:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:8:2.english: Since [she] becomes weak - If one feeds a person's blood to a cat, that person becomes weak.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:9:1.hebrew: הא - דתנא: כל הכשר להצניע, ויש בו שיעור שרוב ב"א עשויין להצניע כשיעור הזה — חייב כל אדם על הוצאתו, ואפילו אדם עשיר שאין שיעור זה חשוב לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 75b:9:1.english: This - That [the Mishnah] taught: Anything fit to store, and there is in it a measure that most people are accustomed to store like this measure — every person is liable for carrying it out, and even a wealthy person for whom this measure is not significant.

Rashi on Shabbat 75b:9:2.english: Not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - [This is stated] later, in [the chapter entitled] HaMotzi.

Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:2:1.hebrew: אין עיבוד באוכלין - אין להתיר מכאן מליחת אוכלין, דאסור מדרבנן מליחה בפרק שמונה שרצים (לקמן שבת דף קח:); ואפילו בי"ט אסור, בפ"ק דביצה (דף יא.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:2:1.english: There is no tanning with regard to food - One should not permit the salting of food from here, for salting is prohibited rabbinically in the chapter [entitled] Shemonah Sheratzim (below, Shabbat 108b); and even on Yom Tov it is forbidden, in the first chapter of Beitzah (11a).

Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:3:1.hebrew: השף בין העמודים בשבת חייב - פירש ר"ח דשף העור על העמוד כדי להחליקו, וכן משמע בירושלמי. ורש"י פירש ששף קרקעית שבין עמודי חלונות — ולא נהירא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:3:1.english: One who rubs between the pillars on Shabbat is liable - Rabbeinu Chananel explained that he rubs the hide against the pillar in order to smooth it, and so it implies in the Yerushalmi. And Rashi explained that he rubs the floor that is between the window pillars — and [this] is not clear.

Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:3:2.hebrew: והמסתת את האבן כו' חייב משום מכה בפטיש - אבל משום מחתך וממחק לא מיחייב, דמיירי שכבר היא מרובעת ומתוקנת, אלא שמייפה אותה ועושה בה שירטוטין ויפוי, כעין שעושין עכשיו מסתתי האבנים. ר"י, וכן ריב"א:
Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:3:2.english: "And one who chisels a stone, etc., is liable due to striking a blow with a hammer" - But he is not liable due to [the labor of] cutting or smoothing, for [the Gemara] is dealing with [a stone] that was already squared and prepared; rather, he is embellishing it and making lines and ornamentation on it, similar to what stonecutters do nowadays. [So explained the] Ri, and likewise the Riva.

Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:6:1.hebrew: הרי אלו לאפוקי מדרבי אליעזר דמחייב אתולדה במקום אב - וא"ת: מרישא שמעינן לה, דתנן: "העושה מלאכות הרבה מעין מלאכה אחת אינו חייב אלא אחת"? וי"מ, דה"ק: "מעין מלאכה אחת" — היינו שתי תולדות מאב א', אבל האב ותולדה דידיה מיחייב תרתי; קמ"ל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:6:1.english: "These are" — to exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Eliezer, who renders [one] liable for a subcategory together with a primary category - And if you say: We [already] learn this from the beginning [of the chapter], as we learned [in the Mishnah]: "One who performs many labors of one type of labor is liable for only one [sin-offering]"? And some explain that [one might think] this is what it means: "Of one type of labor" — that is, two subcategories from one primary category; but [for] the primary category and its own subcategory, [one might think that] he is liable for two. [Therefore, the Mishnah here] teaches us [that this is not so].

Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:6:2.hebrew: חסר אחת לאפוקי מדר' יהודה - תימה, דממנינא דרישא שמעינן לה! וליכא למימר תנא ושייר, דהא "אלו" קתני. ומיהו הא ליכא לאקשויי: דהא מ"אלו" דרישא שמעינן לאפוקי מדר' אליעזר — דאיכא למימר דנקט ברישא "אלו אבות" משום דקאי אדקתני לעיל "חייב על כל אב מלאכה". וי"ל, דממנינא דרישא לא שמעינן לאפוקי מדרבי יהודה; דאיכא למימר דלא חשיב אלא מלאכות חשובות, אבל שובט ומדקדק, אע"ג דמלאכות הן, לא קתני להו משום דאינם מבוררות כל כך. וכה"ג משני בפ"ק דקדושין (דף טז:) גבי "אלו מעניקין להן": "דבר שיש לו קצבה קתני, דבר שאין לו קצבה לא קתני":
Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:6:2.english: "Less one" — to exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Yehuda - It is puzzling: For from the count in the opening clause [of the Mishnah], we [already] learn this! And one cannot say that [the Tanna] taught [some] and omitted [others], since [the Mishnah] teaches "these" [indicating an exhaustive list]. However, one cannot raise this objection: that from "these" of the first clause we learn to exclude Rabbi Eliezer — for one could say that [the Tanna] formulated in the first clause "these are the primary categories" because it refers back to what was taught earlier, "one is liable for each primary category of labor." And one can say: That from the count in the opening clause we would not learn to exclude Rabbi Yehuda; for one could say that [the Tanna] counted only prominent labors, but shovet [lining up the warp] and medakdek [beating the woof], even though they are [primary] labors, he did not teach them because they are not so distinct. And the Gemara answers in a similar manner in the first chapter of Kiddushin (16b) regarding "These are the ones for whom one provides severance gifts": "A matter that has a fixed amount, [the Mishnah] taught; a matter that does not have a fixed amount, it did not teach."

Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:8:1.hebrew: לאפוקי עצי אשרה - דלא כרבי יהודה, דאמר בפרק רבי עקיבא (לקמן שבת דף צ.): "אף המוציא משמשי ע"ז כל שהוא — חייב", אלא כת"ק דפליג עליה — כן פירש בקונט' התם. וקשה לרשב"א: הא דקאמר הכא, "מ"ד דם נדה כ"ש עצי אשרה" — מנא ליה? דילמא סבר כרבי יהודה, ומחייב בעצי אשרה, שמצניעין אותן לשריפה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:8:1.english: To exclude the wood of an ashera - [This is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who said in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Akiva" (below, Shabbat 90a): "Even one who carries out accessories of idolatry in any amount is liable"; rather, [it is] in accordance with the first tanna who disagrees with him — so explained the Kuntres [Rashi] there. And the Rashba asks: That which [the Gemara] says here, "The one who said the blood of a menstruating woman, all the more so the wood of an ashera" — from where does [the Gemara] know [this]? Perhaps he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and deems [one] liable for the wood of an ashera, because they store them for burning!

Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:9:1.hebrew: הא דלא כר' שמעון - פירש בקונטרס: הא דתנן "כל הכשר כו'" — שרוב בני אדם עשויים להצניע כשיעור הזה, חייב כל אדם על הוצאתו, אפילו אדם עשיר שאין שיעור זה חשוב לו. משמע מדבריו דלא מחייב ר' שמעון אלא בסתם בני אדם שרגילין להצניעו, שאותו שיעור חשוב להן, ואפילו לא הצניעו הוא. ולקמן פי': "לא נאמרו שיעורים שבמשנה אלא למצניעין אותו קודם לכן, וחזר המצניע והוציאו" — משמע דוקא בהצניעו חייב! ואומר ר"י, דיש ליישב פירושו: דמה שמצריך לקמן הצנעה — היינו לאדם עשיר שאין דרכו להצניע. ומכל מקום, פירוש מילתיה דר"ש צריך לפרש כמו שפירש כאן. דאי מיירי במצניעין לאותו דבר עצמו שמפורש במשנה, כמו שפירש התם — אם כן, כולהו הוה מצי למימר בכל שהוא, בכדי שיפת קילור, כדתנן בפ' המצניע (לקמן שבת צ:) דלרפואה בכל שהוא, ואתיא כר"ש, מדלא קאמר התם בגמ' "הא דלא כר"ש", כי היכי דקאמר (דף צא.) "הא דלא כר"ש בן אלעזר". ומהתם נמי יש לדקדק, דלר' שמעון סתם בני אדם שרגילין להצניעו מיחייבי אפי' לא הצניעו, מדקתני: "המצניע לזרע כו' וכל אדם אין חייבין עליו אלא כשיעורו", משמע בלא הצנעה, וכר"ש נמי אתיא כדפי'. ואין לפרש דבעשיר שאין דרכו להצניע לא מיחייב לר"ש אפי' בהצניעו, דהא אמר בהמוציא יין: "בד"א? במוציא, אבל במצניע — כל שהוא. ר"ש אומר: בד"א? במצניע כו'". ומפרש מצניע דרבנן: בתלמיד שאמר לו כו', דבר שאינו חשוב לכל, אי אצנעיה רביה — אין, אי לא — לא; ודומיא דהכי נראה דהוי מצניע דר"ש, דתליא מילתא באותו שהצניעו, היינו בעשיר. קשה לרשב"א: דמהאי טעמא דקאמר הכא מתני' דלא כר"ש — משום דמתני' סתמא קתני דחייב, משמע שכל בני אדם חייבין עליו, אפי' אותן שאין חשוב להן שיעור זה — מהאי טעמא נמי הוה ליה למימר בההיא דפרק המצניע דהויא דלא כר"ש! ושמא י"ל: דהכא דנקט לפרושי, הוה ליה לפרושי טפי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 75b:9:1.english: This is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: That which we learned [in the Mishnah], "Anything fit [to store]..." — since most people are accustomed to store an amount like this measure, any person is liable for carrying it out, even a wealthy person to whom this measure is not significant. It is implied from his words that Rabbi Shimon deems liable only ordinary people who are accustomed to storing it, for whom that measure is significant, even if he [this individual] did not store it [himself]. Yet later [at the beginning of Perek HaMotzi Yayin, 76b], he explained: "The measures in the Mishnah were stated only for those who stored it beforehand, and the one who stored it then carried it out" — which implies that [one is] liable specifically if he stored it! And the Ri says that his explanation can be reconciled: that that which he requires storage later is with regard to a wealthy person, whose practice is not to store [such a small quantity]. And in any event, the explanation of Rabbi Shimon's statement must be explained as [Rashi] explained here. For if it is dealing with those who store [an item] for that very purpose specified in the Mishnah, as he explained there — if so, for all of them [the Mishnah] could have said [that liability is incurred] in any amount, [such as] in an amount sufficient to spread collyrium [eye salve], as we learned in the chapter [entitled] HaMatzni'a (below, 90b) that for medicinal purposes [liability is incurred] in any amount. And that [Mishnah] accords with Rabbi Shimon, since the Gemara does not state there: "This is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon," just as it states (91a): "This is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar." And from there too it can be deduced that according to Rabbi Shimon, ordinary people who are accustomed to storing it are liable even if they did not store it [themselves], since it teaches: "One who stores [it] for seed etc., and any [other] person is only liable for it [if he carries] its measure," which implies [that they are liable for its measure] without storing [it beforehand]; and it also accords with Rabbi Shimon, as we explained. And one cannot explain that with regard to a wealthy person, whose practice is not to store [it], he is not liable according to Rabbi Shimon even if he stored it; for it was stated in [Perek] HaMotzi Yayin: "In what [case] does this apply? Regarding one who carries out [normally]; but regarding one who stores [it] — [he is liable in] any amount. Rabbi Shimon says: In what [case] does this apply? Regarding one who stores... etc." And [the Gemara] explains "one who stores" according to the Rabbis: in [the case of] a student to whom [his master] said etc., [that regarding] an item that is not significant to everyone, if his master stored it — yes [he is liable], if not — no. And analogous to this, it appears that "one who stores" of Rabbi Shimon [is understood], that the matter depends on that [specific person] who stored it, which refers to a wealthy person. The Rashba poses a difficulty: For based on this reason that [the Gemara] states here that the Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon — because the Mishnah taught generically that one is liable, which implies that all people are liable for it, even those to whom this measure is not significant — for this reason too it should have said with regard to that [Mishnah] in the chapter [entitled] HaMatzni'a that it is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon! And perhaps it can be said: Here, where [the Mishnah] undertook to explain [the principle], it should have explained [it] further:
